prompts.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you’ve had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you’ve taken, or through something else.
prompts.applies_to: Applicants with a first-choice major (not Undeclared)

prompts.prompt: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from Illinois and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them.
prompts.applies_to: Applicants with a first-choice major (not Undeclared)

prompts.prompt: What are your future career or academic goals? You may include courses you took in high school and how these impacted your goals.
prompts.applies_to: Undeclared applicants (replace the first-choice major essays)

prompts.prompt: What are your academic interests? Please include 2-3 majors you’re considering at Illinois and why.
prompts.applies_to: Undeclared applicants (replace the first-choice major essays)

prompts.prompt: Please explain your interest in your second-choice major or your overall academic or career goals.
prompts.applies_to: Applicants who list a second-choice major

intl_finance.document: Financial documents (types not published on the pages read) plus the online I-20 application
intl_finance.notes: Illinois says international applicants do not submit financial verification papers with the application; it requests financial documents and official transcripts only if you are admitted and choose to attend. International students who need an I-20 must submit the online I-20 application (SEVIS codes CHI214F01070000 for F-1, P-1-00209 for J-1). No amount or calendar date is published on these pages.

notes: The essay page is undated: it does not name a cycle, but the same site's international page already refers to fall 2027, so it is treated as the 2026-27 cycle. Each Illinois essay is 'about 150 words' (the word_limit 150 is that approximate figure). The first-year application has 2-3 Illinois essays in the Writing section of the Common App, plus the Common App personal essay (250-650 words), which is not listed here. The checklist (source 3) is the page that sends admitted international students to the I-20 application; the amount of funds and acceptable document types were not found for first-year applicants.
